problem: Purely network-based MultiON agents stack complex memory or world-model modules that overfit and generalize poorly in data-scarce regimes. Naively coupling networks with optimization is fragile, because small-sample predictions are unreliable and partial observability denies the global information needed to formulate the optimization problem.
motivation: Explicit optimization models encode hard task structure and coordinate multiple goals without extra parameters, which should help generalization when data is scarce (e.g. search-rescue). The obstacles are unreliable network predictions and partial observability, so predictions must be turned into calibrated uncertainty sets and planning must be made robust to them.
key_idea: NeuRO trains a perception network end-to-end with a downstream robust pursuit-evasion optimization: PICNN-based conformally calibrated convex uncertainty sets over object transition matrices feed a dualized robust planner, whose solution feeds back as an action offset and a task reward.
insight: The optimizer supplies task structure that the network need not learn, giving faster convergence and better transfer across goal counts (Fig. 3; the train-on-m=1 to eval-on-m=2 drop is -12% vs -17% for OracleEgoMap). The ablations show that (a) a lower conformal coverage level (higher alpha) gives worse prediction error and worse success (80→66), (b) the action blending weight is sensitive, with lambda=0.4 collapsing success to 52 from 80 at lambda=0.2, and (c) a task-tailored S-MON* formulation beats the generic U-MON*-equivalent one by 6 SPL. The learned transition matrix M emerges without direct supervision, driven only by feedback from the optimizer.
method: Neural perception module: CNN on RGB-D plus egocentric map and goal/action embeddings feed a GRU, giving state features f_t and a base policy and value (OracleEgoMap Occ+Obj backbone from MultiON).

Robust optimization planner: MultiON is cast as a pursuit-evasion game on an E×E grid with prior/posterior belief states, a same-cell detection model, and a continuous agent position path; the objective is min over path, max over transition matrices M in the uncertainty set, of the discounted capture belief (S-MON adds a path-length term).

PICNN conformal calibration: a PICNN score g(x,M), convex in M, defines the uncertainty set Ω(x)={M | g(x,M)≤q}, with q the ceil((N+1)(1-α))-th quantile of calibration scores, giving marginal coverage ≥1-α (Proposition 1).
Dual reformulation: the inner max is relaxed to linear constraints and dualized via strong duality, giving a single tractable min problem [U-MON]* / [S-MON]* solvable by convex solvers (CVXPY).

Solution feedback: the optimal trajectory gives an action offset a_task blended as a=λ·a_net+(1-λ)·a_task, the optimal objective is a task reward combined with the env reward through the Goal Vector Method, and gradients flow through KKT implicit differentiation.
Scalability extension: basis-function expansion and sparse kernel approximation reduce optimization cost from O(E²τ) to O(Kτ) (appendix).

setting.backbone: OracleEgoMap-style CNN+GRU RL policy with a PICNN uncertainty head and a convex robust optimization layer (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: MultiON train split, 250k updates (RL with env reward plus optimization task reward); no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus egocentric occupancy/object map (OracleEgoMap) and goal-object vector
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: FORWARD, TURN-LEFT, TURN-RIGHT, FOUND
setting.privileged: Oracle egocentric map (OracleEgoMap Occ+Obj inputs, as in the MultiON baseline)

numbers.extra: unordered variant; only baseline is OracleEgoMap

numbers_note: MultiON is not in the canonical list, so it is mapped to the 'MultiON' name. Only Success/Progress/SPL/PPL are reported. The appendix scalability table (E=20/50/100 with basis expansion, S-MON m=2) gives Success 82/83/85 and is not listed.
results: On S-MON, NeuRO beats the strongest baselines Lyon and HTP-GCN: m=2 Success 80 vs 76 and SPL 66 vs 62; m=3 Success 62 vs 57 and SPL 40 vs 36. On U-MON it beats OracleEgoMap (m=2 Success 62 vs 54, SPL 52 vs 38). It also converges faster and degrades less when transferred across goal counts.
limitations: Relies on convex approximations of uncertainty (PICNN), which cannot fully capture non-convex visual uncertainty.
Solver cost grows with grid size E and horizon τ (quadratic in E); larger grids need approximations and gave no clear gain.
Evaluated only on synthetic MultiON in simulation, with oracle map inputs and no real-robot experiments; the convergence analysis is informal.
